extracted.intended_audience: marketers, advertising professionals, creative directors, and brand managers interested in ad effectiveness and Cannes Lions trends
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for creating and assessing humor-led film advertising (especially award-focused work like Cannes Lions), emphasizing emotional drivers, creative features, and effectiveness metrics. Useful for marketers and agencies optimizing ads for long‑term brand building and award recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test Your Ad star rating (1.0–5.9) — long‑term brand‑building potential
rubrics_metrics.description: System1’s Test Your Ad platform collects viewers’ emotional responses to ads and assigns a score of 1.0 to 5.9 Stars based on long‑term brand‑building potential. Ads that make people feel intense, positive emotions like happiness and surprise score high on the scale. Usually only 1% of ads in the database secure a 5‑Star score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Star rating as a primary effectiveness metric: examples given — Uber’s Silver Lion ad scored 3.8‑Stars (predicts “Good” brand‑building potential); the Sabina Bronze Lion was a 5‑Star result. Treat higher Stars as indicating stronger long‑term brand impact; very few ads reach 5‑Star status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional drivers: happiness and surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ads that make people feel intense, positive emotions like happiness and surprise score high on the scale." "Happiness and surprise yield lasting commercial impact, especially when viewers feel those emotions intensely."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for intense positive emotions — prioritize moments that elicit happiness and surprise to boost long‑term brand effects. Measure emotional intensity in testing, not just presence of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of humor as a strategic element
rubrics_metrics.description: The return of humor in advertising is notable: 75% of US/UK winners used humor in 2024 (up from 52% in 2023). A YouGov/Spikes survey found humor contributed most to recall of favorite ads; award submissions tagged “humor” increased 48% in 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporating humor can increase both recall and award potential. Consider positioning work for humor recognition (tagging/submitting appropriately) and leveraging humor to lift effectiveness above average TV ad levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of humor and trade‑offs (awkward/uncomfortable vs other forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many awarded ads leverage awkward or uncomfortable situations to get laughs, but these scenarios "run the risk of making viewers experience the discomfort too." The article recommends tapping into other ways to get laughs — surreal ads, slapstick ads, and character comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be intentional about the type of humor: avoid relying solely on awkwardness that causes viewer discomfort. Test whether the humor yields happiness/surprise rather than just unease. Diversify comedic approaches (surreal, slapstick, character comedy) to broaden appeal and avoid negative reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right‑brained vs left‑brained creative features (broad‑beam vs narrow‑beam attention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citing Orlando Wood: "right‑brained features capture broad‑beam attention and contribute to long‑term growth. Left‑brained features are more effective at engaging narrow‑beam attention, appealing to those who already have an inherent interest in the brand or product." Judges favored ads with more right‑brained features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize right‑brained creative elements to drive broad attention and long‑term growth when aiming for award and brand impact. Use left‑brained techniques when the goal is targeted engagement or short‑term persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific right‑brained features to favor: characters with agency, storytelling, betweenness
rubrics_metrics.description: Right‑brained features in winning ads included "characters with agency, storytelling and betweenness that conveys connection among characters." The average number of right‑brained features was 6 among the examined winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build narratives with active characters, clear storytelling arcs, and interpersonal connection (betweenness). Aim to include multiple right‑brained features (the winners averaged ~6) to increase broad appeal and judge favorability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left‑brained features to use sparingly: voiceover, split‑screen, strong product focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Left‑brained features observed include "voiceover, split‑screen effect, strong product focus" which tend to engage narrow‑beam attention and are less than half as prevalent as right‑brained features among winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If included, use voiceover, split‑screen, and overt product focus judiciously—they help clear messaging or product demonstration but can reduce broad emotional resonance and long‑term growth potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural and international resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: 2024 winners were more international: 73% of awarded film ads came from outside the US/UK (compared to 51% last year). Winners spanned 16 countries, and some ads (e.g., Sabina) reflect local social norms while entertaining audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cultural specificity and international resonance: local social insights can drive both regional effectiveness and international award recognition. Be mindful of how culturally specific humor will translate across markets; test for cross‑cultural reception where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character‑driven comedy, celebrity casting, and user‑generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples cited: Uber’s ad pairs Asa Butterfield and Robert De Niro (character comedy). Tide’s "You’re Gonna Need More Tide" leverages user‑generated content and comedian Kumail Nanjiani to highlight messy situations that surprise and delight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage strong characters, believable casting or recognizable comedic talent, and authentic UGC where appropriate to create surprise and delight. These elements can boost emotional response and memorability when integrated into a coherent story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award submission/category strategy (tagging and category fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cannes introduced a humor category within Cultural & Context; Adweek reported a 48% increase in submissions tagged with "humor" in 2023. Cannes’ formal recognition of humor means categorying matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming for industry recognition, tag and submit work to relevant categories (e.g., newly introduced humor category) and ensure the entry clearly demonstrates the comedic intent and cultural/contextual relevance.
